items.title: Southern India has grown wetter over seven decades, finds IMD study
points: This zone now covers nearly three-fourths of peninsular India, compared with about three-fifths in the 1950s.

The study, titled ‘Identifying the climate zones shifts of Indian meteorological subdivisions: insights from historical records’, uses the Köppen-Geiger climate classification system to assess changes across India’s meteorological subdivisions.
The researchers mapped India’s climate zones across successive 30-year periods, using the IMD’s rainfall and temperature observations from 1951 to 2020.
They found that most of the shift in southern India had occurred during the two most recent periods, 1981-2010 and 1991-2020, primarily because of an increase in rainfall.
This year, the IMD’s Regional Meteorological Centre in Chennai declared the onset of the northeast monsoon on October 15, 2026, five days ahead of its normal date.

The country as a whole recorded a 12.6% deficit during the season, as El Niño conditions contributed to the weakening of the southwest monsoon.

items.title: Former USS Enterprise Begins Final Voyage to Alabama for Dismantling
points: The former USS Enterprise (CVN 65) departs Newport News Shipbuilding under tow on November 2, 2026, bound for dismantling in Mobile, Alabama.

The former USS Enterprise (CVN 65), the world’s first nuclear-powered aircraft carrier, departed Newport News Shipbuilding in Virginia under tow on Monday, November 2, beginning its final journey to Mobile, Alabama, where the historic warship will be…

The departure marks another milestone in the retirement of one of the U.S. Navy’s most storied vessels, nearly 14 years after the carrier completed its final deployment and almost a decade after its formal decommissioning.
The ship is headed to a commercial dismantling facility in Mobile, where NorthStar Maritime Dismantlement Services will carry out the work under a $418.5 million Navy contract awarded in July 2026.

In 1964, Enterprise participated in Operation Sea Orbit, joining the nuclear-powered cruiser USS Long Beach and destroyer leader USS Bainbridge in a historic around-the-world voyage without refueling.
